learn.title: Text becomes tokens
learn.body: Before processing text, a language model system splits it into tokens. A token may be a word, part of a word or punctuation. The exact split depends on the model, so tokens are not simply a count of words.

learn.title: A finite working context
learn.body: The context is the information available for generating a response, such as instructions, conversation history and supplied material. A context window is its finite token capacity. Its size and the way a product manages it depend on the model and application.

learn.title: Available is not always used
learn.body: Even when information fits, a model can miss or misuse a relevant detail. When the context grows or a new session begins, earlier requirements may no longer be present. Do not assume that a model remembers everything you previously discussed.

learn.title: Continue a habit-tracker task
learn.body: Restore the useful context instead of copying an entire old conversation.
steps: State the goal: add a weekly summary to the habit tracker.
Give the current state: daily entries already save correctly.
Include the decision: a week starts on Monday.
Ask for the next result: propose the summary logic and acceptance checks.

learn.title: Build a compact handoff
learn.body: For later work, restate the goal, relevant facts, decisions and next task. Include only material that helps with that task. Some applications supply conversation history or another state mechanism, but a basic request does not magically retain every earlier exchange.
If an answer ignores an old requirement, check whether that requirement is present and easy to find in the current context.

questions.prompt: Which statement about tokens is correct?
choices: They are pieces of text, not always whole words
Every word always becomes exactly one token
Their meaning is identical across every model
questions.explanation: Tokenization can split a word into parts or treat a short word as one token. The exact result depends on the model.

questions.prompt: A context window has a \_\_ token capacity.
questions.explanation: A context window is finite. The application and model determine its capacity and how earlier material is managed.

questions.prompt: What should you restore when continuing earlier work in a fresh session?
questions.explanation: Restore the relevant goal, facts, decisions and next task. A fresh session should not be treated as though it automatically knows the earlier discussion.

questions.prompt: Match each handoff item to its purpose.
questions.explanation: A compact handoff separates the outcome, existing state, chosen rules and immediate work. Together they restore useful context without unrelated history.

questions.prompt: Put the preparation of a new-session handoff in order.
steps: Select the goal, current state and decisions it needs
Provide the compact context with the request
questions.explanation: Start from the next task so you can select only useful information. Then remove noise and supply the resulting context explicitly.

questions.prompt: A model misses a requirement even though it appears in a long supplied document. What is the best response?
choices: Restate the relevant requirement clearly and check the new answer
Assume the requirement was followed because it fit
Add unrelated history until the window is full
Treat the long document as proof the answer is correct
questions.explanation: Fitting inside a context window does not guarantee that a model will use a detail correctly. Make the relevant requirement easy to find and evaluate the response.
